Revised assessment incorporating SLOOS:
- The FOMC statement is modestly dovish on fundamentals (sub-2% inflation, steady hold at 1.50–1.75%, and continued T-bill purchases/repo ops to keep reserves ample).
- SLOOS points to tighter credit supply and softer demand: banks increased credit score thresholds and tightened credit limits; standards tightened for C&I and construction/land development; several consumer loan categories saw tighter standards and weaker demand; banks expect tighter standards ahead, reduced risk tolerance, and potential deterioration in loan portfolios and collateral values.
- These SLOOS signals validate the statement’s concern about weak business investment and add downside risk via a credit channel, increasing the case for accommodative posture and liquidity support.
- Financial-stability considerations (elevated valuations, leverage) still argue for caution rather than additional easing, but the SLOOS tilt makes the overall read more dovish than previously assessed.

Net: Slightly more supportive than the FSR-only view; nudging the dovish score higher.
